summary: The seven committed changed paths and dedicated workflow edits are allowed, and frozen artifacts are intact. Transport is blocked by two semantic boundary findings: owned-lifetime guard abort lacks explicit diagnostic-not-reached classification, and JSONL evidence is published without an event/content allowlist. Ordinary guard return/error semantics passed pure mocks. This is not a product/native/release verdict.

findings.title: Owned-lifetime abort is not explicitly classified diagnostic-not-reached
findings.requirement: Spec lines 83-91 require the common guard to report its own budget abort as diagnostic-not-reached, not product failure, with exhaustion explicit unknown.
evidence: native-runtime-parity.mjs:92-100 logs owned-lifetime-expired and exits 92, rather than diagnostic-budget-abort.

native-runtime-parity.mjs:305 collects only diagnostic-budget-abort; 307-311 places lifetime expiry only in cleanupUnknownBasis; 317-319 always emits reached:true without a top-level not-reached classification for this path.

controls.json C06 runs the actual extracted runParent function against virtual filesystem/child handles: status=92, reported=null, reached=true, classification absent, guardAborts=[], diagnosticCompleted=false, cleanupUnknown=true with owned-lifetime-expired basis.
findings.observedLimits: The implementation correctly avoids claiming product cleanup failure. The failure is the missing explicit diagnostic provenance/not-reached classification; this report does not claim it emits productFailure=true.
findings.minimumCorrectionBoundary: Within the new CLI only, classify lifetime/watchdog diagnostic aborts explicitly and preserve unknown product result and cleanup as separate fields; do not alter frozen product behavior.

findings.title: JSONL evidence publication bypasses the metadata/content allowlist
findings.requirement: Spec lines 69 and 77 require no raw env/stderr/content and only allowlisted metadata/canary evidence. The approved plan output contract excludes arbitrary stderr, credentials and arbitrary keys.
evidence: native-runtime-parity.mjs:145-151 readRows checks size/JSON parsing only, without event/key/value schema validation.

native-runtime-parity.mjs:125 and 137-138 persist child error.code without a sanitizer. The stdout/stderr canary check at 257-263 does not cover guard/trace bytes.

findings.observedLimits: This proves an unenforced artifact boundary, not actual host secret leakage. All injected content is synthetic and in-memory. Native Windows emitted data and real leakage remain unknown.
findings.minimumCorrectionBoundary: Validate/reconstruct every exported evidence event in the new CLI, reject unknown keys/unsafe values with fail-closed metadata, and never publish unvalidated raw bytes. The frozen old trace implementation must remain unchanged.

verifiedNonViolations.topic: owned handle cleanup versus historical PID inference
verifiedNonViolations.detail: New cleanup targets active owned handles only. Historical PIDs are queried with signal 0 but not killed. Closed handle mock was not signalled. taskkill status 128 is not used to infer whole-tree/product cleanup success or failure. Unknown cleanup and trace health remain explicit and separate.

Only E0-E4 are enumerated; one key per arm is asserted. HOME/USERPROFILE/temp/Git global config are synthetic; inherited environment keys are limited to PATH/SystemRoot/WINDIR/ComSpec/PATHEXT. E4 uses the built-in system module path, not inherited personal PSModulePath. Both forms self-preload the common guard. The output explicitly says old trace off is not uninstrumented original CI; no combined arm is executed.

Parent re-admits immediately before launch with a 40s case plus 3s cleanup/output scheduling reserve. Common worker guard enforces <=38 smoke/<=76 total PowerShell launches and <=10s native budget. Smoke is P0 then P1 then P2, with previous success required. First complete P2 arm per form is selected. Parent cases for both forms precede round-robin remaining analogs. Worst-case reservations are smoke=3, parent=3, confirmation=14, binding=14, healthy=6; 10 smoke cases plus all analogs would reserve 104 launches, so caps intentionally deny some cases rather than raise bounds. Denied cases are recorded. Absolute real-time enforcement under OS/syscall stalls is not proved.

Node22 syntax checks and actionlint passed. Existing exact non-main branch/job guard, contents:read, immutable checkout, no persisted checkout credentials, Node22/npm ci, 12-minute timeout and scoped upload list are retained.

risksAndUnknowns.detail: validProbe accepts a smoke payload with observations=[] and p2Succeeded=true; it does not enforce stage completeness. The injected-parent control also shows empty observations can be marked diagnosticCompleted. Actual runProbe missing its stage observations was not demonstrated, so this is retained as a risk rather than an additional scope violation.

Binding fixture cwd is /allowed/project rather than an owned-root-derived path; product Git enrichment may attempt that fixed outside-root directory. No live Windows filesystem probe was run, so accidental real-path collision and any unrelated data access are not proved. Keep the synthetic-only boundary explicit.

If guard-abort logging is unavailable, product wrappers can replace a worker abort's code with a generic Replay refusal and measure may lack the before/after abort marker. The health path fails closed, but exact abort provenance in that combined failure path was not independently executed here.

No native Windows PowerShell smoke, parent rename/hardlink hook, downstream confirmation/binding/healthy analog, real cleanup tree, real timing, real output, service or network probe was executed. Native coverage, OS behavior, strict 600s elapsed bound and actual leakage are unknown. VM controls do not substitute for native acceptance.
